Subject: Hosted suitability signals + rate/endpoint clarifications

Hi Samira / team,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for walking us through the ClearPath MVP and expected traffic shapes. As promised, a short recap + a few targeted questions so we can validate whether Hosted is the right fit for your first pilot (or if we should surface Dedicated/Private options).

Recap (quick):
- Primary use: customer-facing summarization + contextual search across uploaded docs.
- 1st-month target: low-concurrency interactive flows (mostly single requests per user), but spikes during batch ingest windows.
- Typical prompt sizes: 1.5k tokens avg; some long-document embeddings for retrieval.

Open questions for qualification (would love short answers so we can size the sandbox):
1) Peak concurrent requests during ingest windows? (you indicated bursts, please share highest expected QPS and burst length)
2) Latency SLO target for interactive flows (p95 target)?
3) Data residency / retention constraints for the pilot — will Hosted data-in-transit+at-rest in our standard regions work or do you need a VPC/private deployment from day one?
4) Auth / SSO and SCIM: will your team want to provision via OAuth / SAML or use API keys for the pilot?

What I can confirm up-front for Hosted quickstart:
- We can provision a sandbox endpoint, isolate it to your account, and increase token/throughput caps for the evaluation window.
- We support KV/prefix caching and per-endpoint routing rules; that tends to drastically reduce cost for retrieval-heavy patterns.

Attachments: sample traffic CSV you shared (ClearPath_MVP_traffic_sample.csv) is included in this thread for reference. I've also attached our one-page quickstart guide (Redwood_Hosted_quickstart-guide-v1.pdf).

Suggested next step: if you can reply with the peak burst numbers (+ confirm residency preference), I’ll loop in Karthik (runtime) to propose endpoint concurrency and RPS targets, and Rishi (commercial) to propose an evaluation credit + short mutual action plan.

Thanks — Mina

Thanks Mina — quick answers inline. Really appreciate the clear recap.

> 1) Peak concurrent requests during ingest windows?
We expect 90–120 requests/sec at peak ingest for the bulk doc processing job; bursts can last ~6–12 minutes as nightly jobs land. Interactive traffic is low: ~3–8 concurrent users at any time initially.

> 2) Latency SLO target for interactive flows (p95)?
p95 < 600ms would be ideal, but we can accept up to 1s for the pilot.

> 3) Data residency / retention constraints?
Hosted in US regions is fine for pilot; long-term we may need EU residency for customers in EMEA, but not blocker now.

> 4) Auth / SSO and SCIM?
For pilot, API keys are fine. If pilot goes to production we’ll require SSO and stricter provisioning.

We attached a sample of the ingest CSV (already in the thread) — hope that helps. Can you also give a short note on whether prefix/KV caching would apply to our retrieval pipeline (we expect heavy retriever hits)?

Also, curious about default rate limits on sandbox endpoints and whether we can request temporary higher burst allowances for the nightly job.

–Samira

Samira — perfect, this is super helpful. Short answers + next actions below.

Quick technical guidance (Hosted):
- Burst handling: we can grant a temporary burst allowance on the sandbox for up to 200 RPS for short windows (we typically gate by minute-long burst windows). For 6–12 minute bursts we recommend staging the ingest as rolling jobs across multiple keys/endpoints to avoid hitting minute-level ceilings.
- Interactive p95: Hosted can meet ~600ms p95 for models in the 70B-ish family with SSD-backed KV caching and careful batching; if you need <400ms we should scope dedicated capacity.
- KV/prefix caching: yes — your retriever-heavy pattern maps well to per-endpoint prefix caching. Ingest traffic will benefit most from batching + streaming ingest endpoints to populate caches first, then serve reads against cached keys.
- Endpoint mapping suggestion: 1 endpoint for interactive low-latency (lower token budget, pinned model), 1 separate ingest endpoint optimized for throughput (higher token sizes, streaming).

I’ve attached the quickstart guide with instructions to spin up sandbox endpoints and request temporary burst increases. Karthik — can you confirm the recommended per-endpoint RPS and concurrency knobs based on ClearPath's numbers above? Rishi — any commercial constraints on enabling the 200 RPS temporary burst for an evaluation?

Proposed next step: 30-min technical kickoff early next week where we provision a sandbox endpoint and run a short ingest smoke test (I’ll prepare a minimal mutual action plan). If that works I’ll book with the team once we get times from you.

Thanks — Mina

Hi Samira — looping in quick runtime guidance. Good summary from Mina. Short technical commitments and a commercial note below.

Runtime notes (for the sandbox eval):
- Recommended starting configuration based on your CSV: two endpoints as Mina suggested. For the ingest endpoint we recommend starting with 80 concurrent streams, target sustained RPS ~100 and allow a burst policy up to 200 RPS for 10-minute windows. For interactive endpoint keep concurrency low (6–12) with a smaller model variant pinned for sub-1s p95.
- Prefetch/KV strategy: run an initial ingest pass to populate KV; after that read latencies drop by ~30–50% depending on hit rate.
- Monitoring: we’ll expose token-level latency metrics and a per-endpoint RPS dashboard so you can see if the burst allowance is hit.

Commercial/next steps (Rishi) — we can enable the sandbox burst allowance for the pilot under a short evaluation addendum. Rishi, I’ve CC'd you to confirm trial credit and any short-term SLA implications.
